With inlet dissolved oxygen 8 mg/L, embryonic oxygen consumption lowers the outlet to about 6.5 mg/L, still above the 5-6 mg/L safety line, so it is judged sufficient; if the egg quantity doubles and oxygen demand rises so the outlet approaches 4 mg/L, increase the flow above 50 L/min or add aeration.
map.孵化用水溶氧至少要多少？: What is the minimum dissolved oxygen for incubation water?
map.鱼卵胚胎发育耗氧高，一般要求孵化水体溶氧 ≥ 5~6 mg/L，环道或孵化桶出水: Fish embryos consume a lot of oxygen during development, so incubation water generally requires dissolved oxygen of at least 5-6 mg/L, and the outlet of the channel or hatching jar should not fall below 4 mg/L. Below this level embryonic development slows and deformity and mortality increase; maintain it by increasing inflow or aerating.
map.水体交换率多少合适？: What water exchange rate is appropriate?
map.常用孵化桶/环道每小时交换 2~5 倍水体；卵量大、水温高时取上限。交换率不足会: Common hatching jars and circular channels exchange 2-5 times the water volume per hour; take the upper limit when egg volume is large and water temperature high. Insufficient exchange causes ammonia nitrogen and CO₂ accumulation and lowers dissolved oxygen, a common cause of reduced hatch rate.
